Attract demo exits ONLY on the C= key, then joystick fire starts play - not a core bug and reset was never required. The demo's exit test is BIT $DC01 #$20 at $9390 (keyboard COLUMN 5, not a joystick bit; fire is read elsewhere at $9349), and the game never writes $DC00/$DC02, so the row select is the KERNAL leftover $7F = row 7 -> C= is the only column-5 key. sim: PLAYS to gameplay on the real 1541 AND DOS 1541; was dead in all 3 modes until the CPU learned the undocumented opcodes (SAX/ISC in the crack's decruncher) - see COMPATIBILITY.md. Pure fastload cannot finish it (raw-sector loader), use AUTO/1541. Board retest pending.

sim: title screen PASSES and the ADEPT game board renders - but ONLY with a plain RUN/STOP tap. 'PRESS RUN KEY TO CONTINUE' is JSR $FFE1 at $42B5, i.e. $91==$7F, and KERNAL UDTIM ($F6C7) refuses to store $91 while anything is held in column 1 or 6 - so the BIOS SEND KEYS 'RUN' key ($83 = SHIFT+RUN/STOP, LSHIFT is column 1) can NEVER satisfy it. Use STOP ($03), or the desktop RUN/STOP button. Q quits out. bios_ui.c row 6 relabelled; see COMPATIBILITY.md. Sim used the GAME_PRG RAM preload, so the disk-load path and the rest of the game are untested - board retest pending.

PARTIAL FIX, sim only, board retest owed. Uses NO KERNAL LOAD: its loader reads the drive error channel (TALK 8/TKSA $6F) then OPEN+CHKIN+CHRIN byte-at-a-time, storing each byte with $01=$34 - so fastload cannot serve it, 1541/DOS only. Was dead in BOTH modes at the title because of a link-engine bug, not the disk path: an empty REQ_FETCH poll (type 0x00) still ran the frame-end buffer clear and destroyed the TKSA secondary address, so no channel ever opened and the ACPTR detour spun forever at $DEC8. Fixed in qspi_slave.v (fetch_ann gates the clear). Now loads everything - AORM 31323B@$0801, '8' 368B@$1000, level '1' 12551B@$A000-$D105 under ROM/IO - but STILL does not reach gameplay: after the level load den=0 and the CPU runs away through the stack page ($0191-$01AF). Separate downstream bug, see COMPATIBILITY.md.

Loader hang FIXED (qspi_slave.v empty-REQ_FETCH ate the TKSA secondary - see COMPATIBILITY.md); game now loads everything correctly, AORM verified BYTE-PERFECT in RAM. Second, separate bug still open and now localised: VICE runs this disk fine, and diffing both machines at the SAME instruction ($82CE) shows only 265 differing bytes in 53KB - 256 of them the stack page. The raster IRQ's ONLY $D019 acknowledge ($82A6) is reachable solely by passing through the boot-installed routine at $0100; the handler does CLI inside itself, so once that routine is not what it expects the IRQ never clears, re-enters, and eats 6 bytes of stack per nesting (3 IRQ frame + 3 PHA - exactly the observed 6-byte period) until it destroys the very code the ack needs. Pushes at $0150 from t=41s. NOT a test artefact: forcing VICE to skip the title identically still works.

Loader hang FIXED (qspi_slave.v empty-REQ_FETCH ate the TKSA secondary); game now loads all four files correctly, AORM byte-perfect in RAM. SECOND bug still open, mechanism known but origin NOT localised: the raster IRQ's only $D019 ack ($82A6) is reachable solely through the boot-installed routine at $0100, and the handler does CLI inside itself - so once that routine is wrong the IRQ never clears, re-enters, and eats 6 bytes of stack per nesting (3 IRQ frame + 3 PHA, exactly the observed period) until it destroys the code the ack needs. VICE (x64sc) runs this disk fine and is the oracle. Beware two phase-alignment traps when diffing: $080B fires for BOTH the boot and AORM stubs, and the $0101 operand is a phase stamp (each stub's resident block points one page below its source), not a divergence. Next step: find the first raster IRQ that fails to reach $82A6.
